import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.9

by R. I. Grigorchuk

A group $G$ has property $P$ if, for every finite subset $F \subseteq G$, there are a finite
subset $S \supseteq F$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that the left translates $xS$, for
$x \in X$, are pairwise disjoint, while the right translates $Sx$, for $x \in X$, cover $G$.
Does every group have property $P$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.9»

open scoped Pointwise

/--
Does every group $G$ have the following property? For every finite subset $F \subseteq G$,
there are a finite subset $S \supseteq F$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that
$x_1S \cap x_2S = \varnothing$ whenever $x_1,x_2 \in X$ are distinct, and
$G = \bigcup_{x \in X} Sx$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (F : Set G), F.Finite →
      ∃ (S X : Set G), S.Finite ∧ F ⊆ S ∧
        X.Pairwise (fun x₁ x₂ ↦ ({x₁} * S) ∩ ({x₂} * S) = ∅) ∧
        Set.univ = ⋃ x ∈ X, S * {x} := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.9»
modeling_decisions: Property P is inlined into the theorem so that the required slot remains the file's single declaration.

A left translate xS is represented by the pointwise set product `{x} * S`, while a right translate Sx is represented by `S * {x}`; this preserves the source's deliberate noncommutative left/right asymmetry.
`X.Pairwise` encodes the requirement for all distinct x₁, x₂ belonging to X, and the covering union ranges over the arbitrary set X without imposing finiteness.
The ambient group G on the covering side is represented by `Set.univ`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.9

by R. I. Grigorchuk

(C. Chou). We say that a group $G$ has *property $P$* if for every finite subset $F$ of $G$,
there is a finite subset $S \supset F$ and a subset $X \subset G$ such that $x_1 S \cap x_2 S$
is empty for any $x_1, x_2 \in X$, $x_1 \ne x_2$, and $G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$.
Does every group have property $P$?

Note the left/right asymmetry in the definition: the *left* translates $x S$, $x \in X$, are
pairwise disjoint, while the *right* translates $S x$, $x \in X$, cover $G$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«8.9»

/-- A group $G$ has *property $P$* (in the sense of C. Chou) if for every finite subset $F$
of $G$ there are a finite subset $S \supset F$ of $G$ and a subset $X \subset G$ such that
the left translates $x_1 S$ and $x_2 S$ are disjoint for all distinct $x_1, x_2 \in X$, and
the right translates $S x$, $x \in X$, cover $G$, that is, $G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$. -/
def HasPropertyP (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ F : Set G, F.Finite → ∃ S : Set G, S.Finite ∧ F ⊆ S ∧ ∃ X : Set G,
    X.PairwiseDisjoint (· • S) ∧ ⋃ x ∈ X, S * {x} = Set.univ

/-- Every finite group has property $P$: take $S = G$ and $X = \{1\}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasPropertyP_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : HasPropertyP G := by
  intro F _
  refine ⟨Set.univ, Set.finite_univ, Set.subset_univ _, {1},
    Set.pairwiseDisjoint_singleton _ _, ?_⟩
  simp

/--
(C. Chou). We say that a group $G$ has *property $P$* if for every finite subset $F$ of $G$,
there is a finite subset $S \supset F$ and a subset $X \subset G$ such that $x_1 S \cap x_2 S$
is empty for any $x_1, x_2 \in X$, $x_1 \ne x_2$, and $G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$.
Does every group have property $P$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], HasPropertyP G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.9»

/--
A group $G$ has property $P$ if, for every finite subset $F \subseteq G$, there
are a finite subset $S \supseteq F$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that the
left translates $x_1S$ and $x_2S$ are disjoint whenever $x_1,x_2 \in X$ are

        (∀ x₁ ∈ X, ∀ x₂ ∈ X, x₁ ≠ x₂ → Disjoint ({x₁} * S) ({x₂} * S)) ∧
        Set.univ = ⋃ x ∈ X, S * {x} := by
  sorry
